name: Goal-Line Double Robber
formation: Double Robber Shell vs Goal-Line Heavy I-Form
coverage: Cover 2 Man Rob (Safeties at 8, Corners Over Top)

summary.motive: Protect the goal line without pressing by aligning corners over the top and converting both safeties into eye-keyed robbers who attack every throwing window in front.
summary.keyDefender: FS as the weak-side robber — he sits on the exact lane the goal-line slant must occupy
summary.whyItWorks: Run action freezes the linebackers but changes nothing for chest-keyed robbers, and over-the-top corners remove any fear of a shot behind the robbery.
summary.failureMode: A true max-protect flood with four verticals stretching the over-the-top corners before the robbers can converge.

beats.title: 1. The Over-the-Top Shell
beats.text: Both corners align 9 yards deep directly over their receivers while both safeties sit at 8 as robbers — nothing is pressed, everything is watched.

beats.title: 2. The Fake Moves Linebackers, Not Robbers
beats.text: The dive action pulls both linebackers downhill for a beat, but the safeties key the QB’s chest and eyes instead of the backfield.

beats.title: 3. Double Robbery Reads
beats.text: On the shoulder turn both safeties break simultaneously — one to the seam window, one to the slant lane — while the over-the-top corners erase anything deeper.

beats.title: 4. Slant Picked at Its Break
beats.text: The goal-line slant lands directly in the weak robber’s hands with zero risk taken behind it — the double-robb structure cashes its specialty call.

relations.tell: Corners line up 9 yards deep directly over their receivers instead of pressed at the line — base 2-man never surrenders that much cushion.
